results.title: Clarification Required - Azure VM and Storage Pricing Update from 1 February 2027 - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
# Clarification Required - Azure VM and Storage Pricing Update from 1 February 2027

 $@chin 385 Reputation points 

 2026-10-05T18:54:46.2433333+00:00 

We received an Azure Service Health alert regarding an upcoming pricing update for specific Azure Virtual Machine and Azure Storage services, effective 1 February 2027, across seven Azure regions.

The notification states that pricing will increase by the following percentages:

- West Europe (Amsterdam): 9%

North Europe (Dublin): 17%

France Central: 11%

France South: 11%

Norway East: 9%

Norway West: 9%

Southeast Asia (Singapore): 8%

However, the Service Health notification does not identify the impacted subscriptions, resources, VM SKUs/series, or specific Storage services, which makes it difficult to determine the actual impact on our environment.

The notification also contains the following statement:

> Services excluded from the regional pricing update

For Azure Virtual Machines, it specifically lists the following excluded series:

v1: Bv1, D, Ds, F, Fs, G, Gs, L, NP, HCS

v2: Av2, Amv2, Dv2, Dsv2, Fsv2, Lsv2

v7: Dsv7, Ddsv7, Dlsv7, Dldsv7, Esv7, Edsv7

...

2026-10-05T19:38:25.03+00:00 

Hi @$@chin ,

> Services excluded from the regional pricing update
> 
> The pricing adjustments described above do not apply to the following Azure Virtual Machine series and Azure Storage services: Azure Virtual Machines
> 
> - v1: Bv1, D, Ds, F, Fs, G, Gs, L, NP, HCS
> - v2: Av2, Amv2, Dv2, Dsv2, Fsv2, Lsv2
> - v7: Dsv7, Ddsv7, Dlsv7, Dldsv7, Esv7, Edsv7

Your question:

> For example, would VM series such as Dv4/Dsv4, Dv5/Dsv5, Ev4/Esv4, Ev5/Esv5, and other v4/v5/v6 series be impacted by the pricing increase?

The VM SKUs you listed are affected by the price increase if they are deployed in the Southeast Asia (Singapore) Azure region. As they are not listed in the exclude list.

Your question:

> Is there an official list of all VM series/SKUs that will be impacted by this pricing update?

All VM series/SKUS that are not excluded by the list above in the email.

A full list of Azure VM series/SKUs you can find here: Sizes for virtual machines in Azure

Your question:

> Is there a way to identify the impacted resources in a subscription through the Azure Portal, Azure Resource Graph, Cost Management, or another Azure API?

In the Azure portal you can list all VMs and filter on Azure region and VM SKU (location and size).With PowerShell, Azure Resource Graph such a query should be possible as well.

Just an example to get started with PowerShell. But the command needs some more filter (Where-Objects):

```powershell
 Get-AzComputeResourceSku | Where-Object { $_.Locations -contains "southeastasia" }

```

Your question:

> Will Azure provide a more detailed Service Health notification identifying the impacted resources/SKUs before the pricing change takes effect?

I am pretty sure there will be further notification and updates on this topic. But no idea when and which details.

Your question:

> Is there a list of the specific Azure Storage services/SKUs affected?

All Azure storages/services that are not listed in the excluded list. 

Excluded are the following Azure storage services:

- Azure Container Storage
- Azure Managed Lustre
- Azure NetApp Files – Cross Region Replication SKU
- Blob Features
- Change Feed
- General Block Blob
- Import/Export
- Queues
- Queues v2
- Standard Page Blob
- Storage Actions
- Storage Bandwidth
- Storage Discovery
- Tables
- Transaction Optimized SKU

results.title: Azure VM Price Change - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
2026-10-05T00:37:46.26+00:00 

Price change below will be affected if we have valid Azure VM Reservation or the new price will be applied when reservation was expired?

 Answer accepted by question author 

 2026-10-05T01:24:20.01+00:00 

Hi, 

Existing VM Reserved Instances (RIs) will not be affected by the price increase. Reserved Instances are a pre-purchase of the base VM costs (even if you choose monthly), which is why the price is locked in for the entire 1 or 3 year term. Please see below screenshot from portal:

If you purchase or renew an RI after the price increase takes effect then the purchase price will be higher than it is now for the listed regions and affected VM sizes. Also, if you allow reservation to expire and don't renew/purchase new then the new full Pay-As-You-Go price that is in effect for that region/VM size will apply.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Thanks.

...

For Azure VM reservations, the reservation discount continues through the committed term. Existing reservations remain valid through their term and continue providing discounts for eligible usage.

When the reservation expires, usage moves to pay-as-you-go rates unless another commitment option is selected. For reservations with autorenew turned on, a replacement reservation is purchased automatically when the reservation expires. If autorenew is off, the billing discount expires and resources are billed at the pay-as-you-go price.

So, a VM price increase does not change the discount on an active reservation during its valid term. The new pricing matters when the reservation expires and the workload falls back to pay-as-you-go, or when a new reservation or renewal is purchased under the then-current pricing.

The answer from Azure Support, in case you stumble across this thread:

Regarding Azure Storage, the pricing adjustment applies to specific Azure Storage services and SKUs rather than generally to all services associated with a StorageV2 (general-purpose v2) account.

For Object/Blob Storage, the affected services include General Block Blob v2 and General Block Blob v2 Hierarchical Namespace, along with other specified Blob Storage SKUs.

For Azure Files, the affected services include Files, Files v2, Premium Files (v1), Azure Files Provisioned v2, File Sync, and applicable Reserved Capacity offerings. However, the Transaction-Optimized SKU (“Standard”) is excluded from this regional pricing adjustment.

results.title: Microsoft for Startups says GPU quota is outside its support scope — but Microsoft Learn says otherwise - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
I am a Microsoft for Startups customer trying to obtain additional A10 GPU quota/capacity for model training.

I opened a Microsoft for Startups support request (TrackingID#2609280050000940). The support engineer told me that Microsoft for Startups Support cannot override Azure GPU capacity limitations and that the GPU quota request needs to continue through the Azure Capacity support channel. I was also told that there is no escalation path through Microsoft for Startups that can override or guarantee additional GPU quota.

I understand that Microsoft for Startups may not be able to approve or override Azure capacity decisions. That is not the issue I am raising.

The issue is that the current Microsoft Learn documentation says something materially different. The page Microsoft for Startups Program Support, last updated June 2, 2026, explicitly lists:

> Azure quota or quota increase requests

under the requests that Microsoft for Startups Program Support directly owns and resolves. It also lists GPU-related benefit requests (coordination) and says Startup Technical Enablement provides quota, GPU, and AI infrastructure alignment.

Documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/startups/microsoft-for-startups/mfs-program-support

results.title: Upgrading the VPN gateway from VPNGw1 to VPNGw1AZ - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
Yes, it will be migrated automatically. You do not need to do anything. From the retirement notice:

> We'll be seamlessly migrating all the gateways on VpnGw1-5 (Non-AZ SKUs) to VpnGw1-5 (AZ SKUs) between April 2025 to October 2026.

The error you are seeing is that migration, not a fault. The retirement date passed on 30 September, so your gateway is now inside the platform migration and will not accept changes while it runs. From VPN Gateway SKU consolidation and migration:

> Existing VPN gateways not supported by an availability zone will no longer allow configuration changes. If you attempt any management or configuration operation, you'll get an error message. This is expected behavior after the rollout.

So there is no manual update to perform, and retrying will return the same message.

Your target SKU is VpnGw1AZ, which you had already worked out. The mapping from the same article:

There is no downtime: "This migration is seamless, and there's no expected downtime during migration."

To confirm when it has finished, look for the AZ suffix on the SKU name, either in the portal under Configuration or with:

```azurecli
az network vnet-gateway show --name "vpn-gateway" --resource-group "test-rg" --query "sku.name"

```

One thing to expect: the new pricing starts only after your gateway is migrated, not before. AZ SKU prices were reduced as part of this consolidation.

results.title: hasta cuando se puede facturar servicio de Azure sobre un contrato EA vencido? - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
Azure under a commercial Enterprise Agreement does not have a fixed 30, 60, or 90-day billing cutoff after the EA expires.

For a commercial EA, the enrollment normally moves to Indefinite Extended Term after the agreement end date. Azure services can continue running and usage continues to be billed until the subscriptions are renewed, transferred, or cancelled. Microsoft states that pricing during this period changes to retail rates, and unused Azure Prepayment generally expires when the enrollment ends. Microsoft Learn

Microsoft also explicitly says that the normal Extended Period Term opt-out process does not stop Azure services after EA expiration; Azure continues to be provided and billed. To stop future Azure charges, the Azure subscriptions/services must be cancelled or transferred appropriately. Microsoft Learn

Azure can continue to be billed indefinitely after a commercial EA expires, as long as Azure subscriptions remain active under the Indefinite Extended Term. There is no automatic short grace-period cutoff.

results.title: Upgrading storage account from V1 to V2 - Microsoft Q&A
highlights:
Yes, your v1 storage accounts need to be upgraded to avoid service disruption. If you don't upgrade them Microsoft will automatically migrate them to v2 after October 13th, 2026.

...

Yes. Upgrading GPv1 to GPv2 is mandatory.

Microsoft will retire general-purpose v1 (GPv1) storage accounts on October 13, 2026. All GPv1 accounts must be upgraded to GPv2 before that date to avoid service disruption.

If a GPv1 account is not upgraded by the retirement date, Microsoft will automatically upgrade it to GPv2. It does not remain on GPv1 indefinitely after retirement.

Key points:

1. GPv1 cannot continue as-is after retirement.
2. Automatic upgrade will occur for remaining GPv1 accounts.
3. Data is preserved during the upgrade.
4. The upgrade is non-disruptive, with the same endpoint names retained.
5. After upgrade, billing changes to GPv2 pricing, which can be different from GPv1.
6. The upgrade is permanent and cannot be reverted back to GPv1.
